Counsel for Petitioner :- Vishnu Pandey,Ayush Mittal Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Siddhartha Varma,J.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.
When land of the petitioner was acquired after a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued, award was finally published on 25.07.2015.

Learned counsel for the petitioner states that advantages which were flowing out of the new Act i.e. Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 were not extended to the petitioner.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Aggrieved by the award a reference was filed by the petitioner on 21.03.2017.

Learned counsel for the petitioner states that benefits which were flowing out of Chapters 5, 6 and 7 of the 'Act, 2013'
were inadvertently not mentioned in the reference and therefore the amendment application was Shri Kashi Jeevdaya Vistarini Gaushala ... vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154182327/
1 filed.

entities.text: Shri Kashi Jeevdaya Vistarini Gaushala ... vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the application was turned down the instant writ petition was filed.

3. Learned Standing Counsel states that there was no requirement for the amendment in the reference and infact if there were benefits which were to be extended to the petitioner because of the provisions of the 'Act, 2013' then they would be considered by the reference Court.

4. Under such circumstance, we provide that even if the amendment is not made to the reference and, if the petitioner presses for the benefits which were flowing from the provisions of Chapters 5,6 and 7 of the 'Act, 2013' then they shall be considered in accordance with law.
5. Under such circumstance the writ petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
